events.description: Registration is required. Click this link to attend the virtual event. In a fast-paced world that often leaves us feeling overwhelmed and disconnected, true healing does not come from looking outward—it begins within. Join us for a transformative virtual conversation with Indigenous Medicine Woman Asha Frost as she explores her groundbreaking book, You Are the Medicine: 13 Moons of Indigenous Wisdom, Ancestral Connection, and Animal Spirit Guidance. The Medicine you have been searching for lives within you. Follow the path of the 13 Ojibwe Moons with Animal Spirits and Ancestors as your guides as you unlock your connection to your own unique, inherent healing power. Through storytelling, ceremonies, and Shamanic journeys, learn to apply ancient wisdom to your life in ways that are respectful and conscious of the stolen lands, lives, and traditions of Indigenous peoples. Discover how to: - Ground and root into your own lineage and meet your Ancestral guides. - Practice self-care and rest on your journey. - Return to Ancestral ways of cleansing and purifying. - Trust and surrender so you can manifest and thrive. - Release self-doubt, fear, disconnection, and insecurity. Register now and take the first step toward recognizing and reclaiming your innate wisdom. Not able to attend live? You can access the recording for this event and all Online Author Series events on our website shortly after they conclude. About the Author: Asha Frost (she/her) is an Indigenous Medicine Woman and a member of the Chippewas of Nawash First Nation. She is from the Crane Clan, the totem of leadership, and believes in holding space from vision and heart. As an energy healer, homeopath, and mentor, Asha has guided thousands of people through profound and lasting transformation. Impacted by generational trauma and colonization, Asha has been on a lifelong journey of reclamation. A lupus diagnosis sent her on a path of studying and practicing a multitude of energy Medicine modalities with many guides. She has blended this life experience with her innate gifts and the wisdom of her Ancestors. She loves sharing her Medicine in powerful ways through Ceremonies, teachings, and speaking events. Through this work, she loves seeing people reclaim their roots, find their healing wisdom, and rise into their power. Asha lives on Anishinaabe, Huron-Wendat, and Haudenosaunee Territory, with her husband and two beautiful children, with whom she co-creates a better world for the seven generations to come. events.title: Mastering MEDICARE: Turn Confusion into Confidence
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Join us for a free, beginner-focused educational session that explains Medicare parts, enrollment timelines, and coverage options. This is an opportunity to get expert insights and clarity on how the latest Medicare updates will affect you. Whether you're new to Medicare, nearing eligibility, or already enrolled, this seminar will help you understand everything you need to know to make informed decisions about your coverage. In this comprehensive discussion, we’ll explore critical topics about Medicare, such as: The ABCs (and D): Breakdown of Part A (hospital), Part B (medical), Part C (Advantage), and Part D (prescription drugs). Eligibility & Timelines: Critical enrollment windows (like the Initial Enrollment Period) to avoid late penalties. Plan Comparisons: Differences between Original Medicare, Medicare Supplement (Medigap) insurance, and Medicare Advantage. Cost Management: Review of premiums, deductibles, and strategies to lower out-of-pocket expenses. Medicare Qualifications: An overview of the eligibility requirements for Medicare, including age, disability, and any other special conditions. Cost & Penalties: Information on Medicare premiums, deductibles, co-pays, and the penalties for late enrollment. Medicare vs. Employer coverage: How Medicare works alongside employer health insurance and when to consider enrolling in Medicare if you’re still working. Don’t miss out on this crucial opportunity to understand how Medicare will change in 2027 and how those changes impact you. Whether you're just starting to navigate Medicare or need a refresher, this seminar is designed for everyone! This workshop will be led by Claudette G. Klein. About the Presenter: Ms. CLAUDETTE G. KLEIN is the owner and CEO of KLEIN FINANCIAL SERVICES, a full-service, financial services firm with a primary focus on health and wealth protection, and life coverage planning. events.title: How Money Became God: Rethinking Wealth and Greed in Modern Society with Paul Vigna
events.description: Registration is required. Click this link to attend the virtual event. Join us for an eye-opening conversation with veteran journalist Paul Vigna as we examine his provocative book, The Almightier: How Money Became God, Greed Became Virtue, and Debt Became Sin, in which he explores the question: how did money go from a tool of commerce into the dominant faith of modern society? In The Almightier, Vigna takes readers on a sweeping historical journey from Renaissance Florence to today’s global financial markets, revealing how wealth accumulation evolved from a moral failing into an unspoken civic virtue. He uncovers the forgotten history of money, tracing the uneasy and often accidental alliance between wealth and religion as it developed from ancient city-states to today’s secular world, where religious devotion has receded and greed has stepped in to fill the void. Through engaging anecdotes, original research, and fresh perspectives on the causes of the many challenges we face today, Vigna makes a compelling argument that money has no power apart from the power we give it. Whether you are interested in economic history, personal finance, or the hidden cultural forces shaping modern life, this talk is sure to pique your interest. Register today to learn more about how devotion to money has replaced religion as the foundation of our society. Not able to attend live? You can access the recording for this event and all Online Author Series events on our website shortly after they conclude. About the Author: Paul Vigna is an author, journalist, editor and speaker, with a particular focus on capital markets and cryptocurrencies. He is the author of Guts: The Anatomy of The Walking Dead and coauthor of The Age of Cryptocurrency and The Truth Machine. For 25 years, he was a reporter and editor for Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal, pioneering coverage of the cryptocurrency sector. He has appeared on CNN, CNBC, MSNBC, Fox, and PBS. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.

events.title: Classical Guitar Performance with Peter Fletcher
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Join us for an evening of classical guitar music with critically acclaimed recording artist and performer Peter Fletcher. Peter Fletcher is an American classical guitarist based in Detroit and New York City. His recordings on the Centaur Records and Towerhill Recordings labels have been critically acclaimed. He is a graduate of the Eastman School of Music. Peter offers an audience friendly, solo recital including repertoire that runs the gamut from the Renaissance Period through the 20th Century. About the Performer: Peter Fletcher began guitar study at the age of seven and was the youngest student to perform in a 1980 master class led by maestro José Tomás, Andrés Segovia’s teaching assistant in Spain. He furthered his studies in master classes with David Leisner, David Russell, Oscar Ghiglia and Pepe Romero, and received his Master of Music degree from the Eastman School of Music in 1995. In demand as a performer at cultural venues throughout the country, Fletcher made his New York debut at Weill Recital Hall at Carnegie Hall in 2007 and returned for performances in 2008, 2009, 2010, 2013 and 2017. His many radio and television appearances have included National Public Radio (NPR) and WABE in Atlanta. Fletcher’s recordings include an all-Grieg album featuring his own guitar transcriptions, released on Centaur Records in 2014, On Tour (2016), and In Concert (2025), featuring music by Sor, Villa-Lobos, Tárrega, Scarlatti, Albéniz and other composers. He continues to perform solo recitals throughout the country. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.

events.title: We Will Receive Justice: Native Histories of the Collapse of the California Missions
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Join us for an illuminating talk on California indigenous history with Gustavo Flores and Lee Panich, co-authors of We Will Receive Justice: Native Histories of the Collapse of the California Missions. We Will Receive Justice explores how Native people in the southern San Francisco Bay Area—the ancestors of today’s Ohlone community—navigated the collapse of the California mission system. The volume spans from Mexican independence in 1821 through the region’s annexation by the United States in 1846, as Native people from Mission Santa Clara and Mission San José fought for emancipation and restitution amid rapidly changing colonial circumstances. The narrative is driven by a reexamination of archives related to the Pueblo of San José, the territorial capital of Monterey, and early U.S. court cases regarding Mexican-era land grants, contextualized through an in-depth analysis of mission records that illuminate the complex social connections of Native individuals and families. We Will Receive Justice offers an ethnohistorical lens for viewing the Indigenous history of Mexican California, examining not simply the history of colonization but how Native people drew on cultural traditions and social relationships to create new lives for themselves in the wake of the Franciscan mission system. About the Presenters: Gustavo Flores received his M.A. in Applied Anthropology from San Jose State in 2014. In addition to teaching courses at SJSU, he also teaches courses at Evergreen Valley College and Mission College. He is currently conducting archaeological research with researchers from Stanford University, using primary sources to understand the past of the indigenous peoples of the Bay Area. Lee Panich is an archaeologist and historical anthropologist. In his research and teaching, he uses a combination of archaeological, ethnographic, and archival sources to examine the long-term interactions between California’s Indigenous societies and colonial institutions, particularly the mission system. He has conducted investigations of Native life at various colonial-era sites, including Mission Santa Clara and Mission San José. On these projects, he has been fortunate to partner with members of the Muwekma Ohlone Tribe and other Native Californian communities, scholars from a range of institutions, as well as numerous undergraduate students. events.description: Registration is required. Click this link to attend the virtual event. Grief is not a one-size-fits-all experience, nor is it a linear journey. Join us online for a comforting and deeply practical conversation with grief guide and author Shelby Forsythia as we explore her book, Your Grief, Your Way: A Year of Practical Guidance and Comfort After Loss. Everyone experiences grief differently after the loss of a loved one. Some people find solace in comforting quotes and warm words, while others feel a need to take action—to do something to memorialize their loss. And some benefit from both approaches. Here's a path forward for you, no matter how you process your grief. Y our Grief, Your Way features: Multiple ways to process grief: Find relief through short meditations, mindful reframings, journaling prompts, concrete actions, and more. A year of daily messages of comfort: Each page includes a quote and a short paragraph about grief along with a practical tip--something you can do to tend to your grief. Comfort and practicality in short spurts: Discover strength and support in these bite-size nuggets, since grief reduces the ability to focus. Quotes from a wide range of grievers: Tend to your grief with thoughtful words of people who have been in your shoes. Filled with daily reflections and gentle prompts, this book offers a safe space to explore your feelings, honor your loved one, and reconnect with yourself. Whether you’re searching for moments of comfort, a spark of hope, or simply a reason to keep going, this guide encourages you to move through grief at your own pace—with no timelines and no judgments. Just the grace to heal in your way. Register today to participate in the conversation and gain a gentle companion for your healing journey. Not able to attend live? About the Author: Shelby Forsythia (she/her) is a grief coach, author, and podcast host. events.title: Exile, Memory, and the Meaning of Home: A Conversation with Ana Hebra Flaster
events.description: Registration is required. Click this link to attend the virtual event. What happens when the country you love forces you out, leaving you just 48 hours to abandon everything you’ve ever known? Join us online for an extraordinary online conversation with author and essayist Ana Hebra Flaster as we discuss her sweeping yet deeply intimate memoir Property of the Revolution: From a Cuban Barrio to a New Hampshire Mill Town. Ana Hebra Flaster was six years old when her working-class family was kicked out of their Havana barrio for opposing communism. Once devoted revolutionaries themselves but disillusioned by the Castro government’s repressive tactics, they fled to the US. The permanent losses they suffered—of home, country, and loved ones, all within forty-eight hours—haunted her multigenerational family as they reclaimed their lives and freedom in 1967 New Hampshire. There, they fed each other stories of their scrappy barrio—some of which Hebra Flaster has shared on All Things Considered— to resurrect their lost world and fortify themselves for a daunting task: building a new life in a foreign land. Weaving pivotal events in Cuba–US history with her viejos’ —elders’—stories of surviving political upheaval, impossible choices, and “refugeedom,” Property of the Revolution celebrates the indomitable spirit and wisdom of the women warriors who led the family out of Cuba, shaped its rebirth as Cuban Americans, and helped Ana grow up hopeful, future-facing—American. But what happens when deeply buried childhood memories resurface, demanding an adult’s reckoning? Here’s how the fiercest love, the most stubborn will, and the power of family put nine new Americans back on their feet. Register today to gain a deeper, more personal perspective on the refugee experience and the enduring quest to define home. Not able to attend live? You can access the recording for this event and all Online Author Series events on our website shortly after they conclude. About the Author: Ana Hebra Flaster is journalist and the author of Property of the Revolution: From a Cuban Barrio to a New Hampshire Mill Town, published in April 2025 (She Writes Press, Simon and Schuster distribution). A former child-refugee from Cuba, Ana’s work has appeared in national print and online media, including: The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Post, and The Boston Globe. Her commentaries and storytelling have aired on NPR’s All Things Considered and PBS’s Stories from the Stage. Since its publication in April 2025, Property of the Revolution has won first place in several international writing contests, including: 2026 IBPA Book Awards (Memoir); 2025 Discovery Book Awards (Nonfiction overall); 2025 International Book Awards (Creative Nonfiction), and the 2025 IAP Book Awards (Memoir of the Year). The memoir was selected as the Nashua, New Hampshire, 2026 All-City Read and the Rivier University 2025 First-Year Read. Ana speaks regularly with student, library, and civic groups about her family’s journey and the refugee and immigrant experience. She is currently focused on covering the struggle for democracy and human rights in Cuba in her weekly Substack, CubaCurious, a project she launched in July 2024. events.title: Online Author Talk : Asha Frost
events.description: In a fast-paced world that often leaves us feeling overwhelmed and disconnected, true healing does not come from looking outward—it begins within. Join us for a transformative virtual conversation with Indigenous Medicine Woman Asha Frost as she explores her groundbreaking book, You Are the Medicine: 13 Moons of Indigenous Wisdom, Ancestral Connection, and Animal Spirit Guidance. The Medicine you have been searching for lives within you. Follow the path of the 13 Ojibwe Moons with Animal Spirits and Ancestors as your guides as you unlock your connection to your own unique, inherent healing power. Through storytelling, ceremonies, and Shamanic journeys, learn to apply ancient wisdom to your life in ways that are respectful and conscious of the stolen lands, lives, and traditions of Indigenous peoples. Discover how to: - Ground and root into your own lineage and meet your Ancestral guides. - Practice self-care and rest on your journey. - Return to Ancestral ways of cleansing and purifying. - Trust and surrender so you can manifest and thrive. - Release self-doubt, fear, disconnection, and insecurity. Register now and take the first step toward recognizing and reclaiming your innate wisdom. About the Author: Asha Frost (she/her) is an Indigenous Medicine Woman and a member of the Chippewas of Nawash First Nation. She is from the Crane Clan, the totem of leadership, and believes in holding space from vision and heart. As an energy healer, homeopath, and mentor, Asha has guided thousands of people through profound and lasting transformation. Impacted by generational trauma and colonization, Asha has been on a lifelong journey of reclamation. A lupus diagnosis sent her on a path of studying and practicing a multitude of energy Medicine modalities with many guides. She has blended this life experience with her innate gifts and the wisdom of her Ancestors. She loves sharing her Medicine in powerful ways through Ceremonies, teachings, and speaking events. Through this work, she loves seeing people reclaim their roots, find their healing wisdom, and rise into their power. Asha lives on Anishinaabe, Huron-Wendat, and Haudenosaunee Territory, with her husband and two beautiful children, with whom she co-creates a better world for the seven generations to come.

Lockhart as we reflect on her impressive body of work, including the literary sensation We Were Liars, and even gain an exclusive sneak peek into her shimmering new thriller, The Pools. Once, in a small New England town known for its hot springs, something terrible happened. Something that should have been a warning to stay away from the pools, if the stories were to be believed. events.title: Online Author Talk : Kelly and Zach Weinersmith
events.description: Join us for an out-of-this-world virtual conversation with New York Times bestselling authors Kelly and Zach Weinersmith as they dive into their book, A City on Mars: Can We Settle Space, Should We Settle Space, and Have We Really Thought This Through? Earth is not well. The promise of starting life anew somewhere far, far away—no climate change, no war, no doomscrolling—beckons, and settling the stars ﬁnally seems within our grasp. Or is it? Critically acclaimed, bestselling authors Kelly and Zach Weinersmith set out to write the essential guide to a glorious future of space settlements, but after years of research, they aren’t so sure it’s a good idea. In a world hurtling toward human expansion into space, A City on Mars investigates whether the dream of new worlds won’t create nightmares, both for settlers and the people they leave behind. In the process, the Weinersmiths answer every question about space you’ve ever wondered about, and many you’ve never considered: Can you make babies in space? Should corporations govern space settlements? What about space war? Are we headed for a housing crisis on the Moon’s Peaks of Eternal Light—and what happens if you’re left in the Craters of Eternal Darkness? Why do astronauts love taco sauce? Speaking of meals, what’s the legal status of space cannibalism? With deep expertise, a winning sense of humor, and art from the beloved creator of Saturday Morning Breakfast Cereal, the Weinersmiths investigate perhaps the biggest questions humanity will ever ask itself—whether and how to become multiplanetary. Register today to be a part of the discussion! About the Authors: Zach Weinersmith is best known as the cartoonist of the comic Saturday Morning Breakfast Cereal. He also co-wrote the bestselling science books Soonish and A City on Mars with his wife, and worked with the artist Boulet to create a children's retelling of the story of Beowulf called Bea Wolf. Dr. Kelly Weinersmith is an adjunct faculty member at Rice University, and is currently President of the Helminthological Society of Washington and the American Society of Parasitologists. Her research on animal behavior and parasites has been featured in The Atlantic, National Geographic, BBC World, Science, Nature, and more. Kelly co-wrote the New York Times bestsellers Soonish: Ten Emerging Technologies That'll Improve And/Or Ruin Everything and A City on Mars: Can We Settle Space, Should We Settle Space, and Have We Really Thought This Through?. In 2024, she and her co-author/husband Zach received a Hugo Award and the Royal Society Trivedi Book Prize for A City on Mars. Kelly is also co-host of the podcast Daniel and Kelly’s Extraordinary Universe.

events.title: Online Author Talk : Paul Vigna
events.description: Register here and submit your questions for the author before the event begins. Join us for an eye-opening conversation with veteran journalist Paul Vigna as we examine his provocative book, The Almightier: How Money Became God, Greed Became Virtue, and Debt Became Sin, in which he explores the question: how did money go from a tool of commerce into the dominant faith of modern society? In The Almightier, Vigna takes readers on a sweeping historical journey from Renaissance Florence to today’s global financial markets, revealing how wealth accumulation evolved from a moral failing into an unspoken civic virtue. He uncovers the forgotten history of money, tracing the uneasy and often accidental alliance between wealth and religion as it developed from ancient city-states to today’s secular world, where religious devotion has receded and greed has stepped in to fill the void. Through engaging anecdotes, original research, and fresh perspectives on the causes of the many challenges we face today, Vigna makes a compelling argument that money has no power apart from the power we give it. Whether you are interested in economic history, personal finance, or the hidden cultural forces shaping modern life, this talk is sure to pique your interest. Register today to learn more about how devotion to money has replaced religion as the foundation of our society. About the Author: Paul Vigna is an author, journalist, editor and speaker, with a particular focus on capital markets and cryptocurrencies. He is the author of Guts: The Anatomy of The Walking Dead and coauthor of The Age of Cryptocurrency and The Truth Machine. For 25 years, he was a reporter and editor for Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal, pioneering coverage of the cryptocurrency sector. He has appeared on CNN, CNBC, MSNBC, Fox, and PBS.

events.description: Register here and submit your questions for the author before the event begins. Step into a sprawling world of celestial magic, political intrigue, and ancient prophecies with New York Times bestselling author Rebecca Roanhorse as we dive deep into her acclaimed Between Earth and Sky trilogy. Black Sun, Fevered Star, and Mirrored Heavens are inspired by the rich and diverse cultures of the pre-Columbian Americas, reshaping modern speculative fiction with unmissable worldbuilding. Black Sun, the first book in the trilogy, introduces us to the holy city of Tova. The winter solstice is usually a time for celebration and renewal, but this year it coincides with a solar eclipse, a rare celestial event proscribed by the Sun Priest as an unbalancing of the world. Meanwhile, a ship launches from a distant city bound for Tova and set to arrive on the solstice. The captain of the ship, Xiala, is a disgraced Teek whose song can calm the waters around her as easily as it can warp a man’s mind. Her ship carries one passenger. Described as harmless, the passenger, Serapio, is a young man, blind, scarred, and cloaked in destiny. As Xiala well knows, when a man is described as harmless, he usually ends up being a villain. Whether you are a longtime fan of the trilogy or searching for your next immersive fantasy read, this is an event you won’t want to miss out on. Register today to go behind the scenes with one of speculative fiction's most exciting voices! About the Author: Rebecca Roanhorse is a New York Times bestselling and Nebula, Hugo, and Locus Award-winning speculative fiction writer. She has published multiple award-winning short stories and novels, including two novels in The Sixth World series, Star Wars: Resistance Reborn, Race to the Sun for the Rick Riordan imprint, and the Hugo Award-winning epic fantasy trilogy Between Earth and Sky. She was the guest editor of America’s Best Science Fiction and Fantasy (2023) and a contributor to the New York Times “100 Best Books of the 21st Century.” She has also written for Marvel comics and games, and her TV writing includes FX’s A Murder at the End of the World, and the Marvel series Echo for Disney+. She has had her own work optioned by Paramount, Amazon Studios, Netflix, and AMC Studios.

events.title: Suminagashi: The Art of Floating Ink
events.description: Suminagashi is a 900-year-old Japanese marbling art. Touch ink to still water, watch it drift into rings and ripples, then lift the pattern onto paper. No two prints are ever the same. This workshop is an invitation to slow down and practice mindfulness. You can’t force the ink, so you learn to breathe, observe, and let things unfold. There’s no right way to do it and no experience needed, which makes it a gentle break from screens, busy thoughts, and perfectionism. Many people find the process calming, and making something with your hands is a simple way to care for your mind. You’ll begin with a short introduction and a guided breathing warm-up, then create several prints to take home. All materials provided. Open to all levels.

events.title: Sound Bath Healing Meditation
events.description: Gaby Castro-Moroder is BACK for another Sound Healing session! Come join us! Sound and music is used as a method of healing across various mediums. After being told for years that she has a healing presence, Gaby Castro started her sound healing journey and took certification courses in tuning forks, crystal sound bowls, and Tibetan sound bowls. Now she provides sound healing group and individual sessions under the name Song Pine and Stone, bringing her gentle presence to those in need. A group sound healing session runs about 60-90 minutes and includes the use of crystal sound healing bowls, Tibetan bowls, tuning forks, and various other sound healing instruments. Attendees will bring their own yoga mats, blankets, pillows, and whatever else they need to be comfortable during the session. Instruments will be played to create a sound bath and attendees will be encouraged to relax and enjoy the soft, soothing sounds. When the session ends, attendees will be asked to rehydrate and we’ll discuss how the session felt for everyone. Age Range: Adults and Seniors NOTE: A consent form may be required and provided at the event. Attendees need to consult with their physician and get approval to attend healing sessions if they have metal in their bodies, suffered concussions, have a pacemaker, use an insulin pump, and the like. Bring your Trick-or-Treat Bags and costumes for a Halloween fun filled day.This event is free and open to the public. Click HERE to view Trick or Treat stops and merchant offers!

events.title: Día de Los Muertos Celebration
events.description: NOVEMBER 1, 2026  Join the festivities as Santana Row hosts a very special tribute to Día de Los Muertos on Sunday, November 1st! The holiday is a time to remember loved ones that have passed, while we embrace our eternal connections. This is a free community event featuring face painting, Catrina and Catrin meet & greets, mariachi music, crafts, and a pop-up market.Entertainment Schedule:10:30 AM – 10 PM: Brunch at Zazil & contribute to the Community Ofrendas (Altars)12 – 5 PM: Cultural Pop-Up Market12 – 3 PM: Día de los Muertos Catrina Photo Ops in Oak Tree Lounge (by Blue Bottle Coffee)12 – 3 PM: Face Painting in Santana Row Park1 – 3 PM: Mariachi & Dance Performances in Santana Row Park3– 4:30 PM: Mariachi & Face Painting at El Jardín Tequila Bar4:30 – 6 PM: Mariachi at Zazil

events.title: Cielo Hotel Valencia Rooftop Holiday Experience
events.description: NOVEMBER 27, 2026  Beginning November 27, join us Tuesday through Saturday from 5:00–9:00 pm, for winter evenings at Cielo Rooftop at Hotel Valencia. The experience will be closed Sundays and Mondays.This holiday season, Cielo Rooftop transforms into an intimate winter retreat high above Santana Row, where seasonal warmth and elevated style come together against the backdrop of the Santa Cruz Mountains. Settle in beneath the open sky and enjoy seasonal cocktails and a curated menu of winter-inspired bites in a warm and inviting rooftop setting. Thoughtful seasonal touches and the glow of the city below create the perfect atmosphere for festive gatherings, date nights, or simply savoring the season.Click HERE for details!

events.title: Spirit of The Row
events.description: DECEMBER 1, 2026  Get in the Spirit of The Row! Join us for the first 3 Tuesdays in December from 6pm-8pm leading up to Christmas, for a live holiday show featuring local arts and community groups, Snow Showers in Park Valencia, photos with Santa, balloons, and more.Spirit of The Row Dates: December 1st, 8th, & 15th.Spirit of The Row Line Up to be announced soon!

events.title: Photos with Santa Claus
events.description: DECEMBER 1, 2026  Get into the holiday spirit with free photos with Santa and Mrs. Claus in the Oak Tree Lounge (in front of Blue Bottle) on December 1, 8, and 15 from 6pm–8pm during Spirit of The Row—capture a festive moment with the merry duo!

events.title: Cars & Croissants on The Row
events.description: DECEMBER 13, 2026  Join us on Sunday, December 13th from 9am-12pm for the 100|OCT Cars and Croissants on The Row! Experience one of the world’s premier exotic car gatherings, featuring an impressive display of supercars, luxury vehicles, and exotic marques from renowned manufacturers.Whether you’re a dedicated car enthusiast or simply looking for a fun morning out, enjoy the opportunity to see incredible vehicles up close, connect with fellow automotive fans, and take in the vibrant atmosphere of Santana Row.This event is FREE to attend. If you’d like to showcase your vehicle, click HERE to reserve a car display space. We look forward to seeing you on the Row!

events.title: Dracula
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Sink your teeth into the ultimate Halloween thrill. Steven Dietz’s adaptation of the timeless classic seduces with elegance and suspense, turning the legendary vampire tale into a high-octane theatrical ride. Bold, chilling, and wickedly smart, the story draws you into a world where reason clashes with superstition and love becomes dangerously intoxicating. This Dracula keeps you leaning forward—never quite sure who holds the power, or what darkness waits just out of sight.

events.title: Alice, Formerly of Wonderland
events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming of age story revealing the truth behind the fairytale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll’s classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria’s youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this acapella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias’ storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn’t always about the fastest draw—it’s about doing the right thing when it counts.

events.title: Beautiful: The Carole King Musical
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Feel the earth move under your feet! Soulful and irresistible, this feel-good musical tells the true story of the woman behind the soundtrack of our lives. From teenage songwriter to chart-topping legend, Carole King finds her voice in a world that wasn’t always ready to hear it. Set against the vibrant music scene of the 1950s and 1960s, the journey follows love, resilience, the sort of friendships that shape a life—and a career that changed music forever. Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including “You’ve Got a Friend,” “It’s Too Late,” and “You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman,” Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.
